subject.title: [voice-call] OpenAI realtime: audio clipping / breaking inside words during first ~30s of outbound calls (Twilio mulaw output)

question: What proof should be required before changing the OpenAI realtime-to-Twilio audio path for this clipping report?
rationale: The source path is clear and user impact is plausible, but current main already avoids the reporter's suspected PCM16-to-mulaw default path, so automation cannot safely choose gain, codec, or pacing changes without live audio evidence.

options.title: Require live diagnosis first
options.body: Keep this issue open until a current-main Twilio/OpenAI call, redacted audio sample, packet capture, or level/queue log isolates the failing layer before any code change.

options.title: Sponsor a focused audio fix
options.body: A maintainer may accept the reporter's reproduction as sufficient and choose a specific owner boundary such as OpenAI format negotiation, codec headroom, or pacer behavior for a narrow PR.

options.title: Close after positive release proof
options.body: Close only if someone can show that v2026.6.11 or current main no longer clips in the reported outbound-call scenario.

recommendation.title: Require live diagnosis first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a current-main Twilio/OpenAI call, redacted audio sample, packet capture, or level/queue log isolates the failing layer before any code change.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely decision spans shared audio codec behavior and realtime telephony pacing, both areas tied to recent steipete-authored or committed history.
